bounded_slice.tested_scope: Exact pinned lbx154/Argus commit 2894b434affaff3a28c1fbbcd5c39f2e7a832236, limited to the production HTTP POST /api/projects/{sid}/tasks route in argus_skill/webapi/routes/workitems.py and its exact alias/delegation chain through argus_skill/webapi/server.py and argus_skill/webapi/mission_items.py into argus_skill/webapi/manager_dispatch.py manager_bounded_handoff. Tested only whether this HTTP task route can reach the bounded handoff with both a generated non-null root_task_id and name_session=true.
observations: The pinned HTTP task endpoint delegates to server_mod.enqueue_task_command with the project/session id and task text.
The pinned server module aliases enqueue_task_command directly to mission_items.enqueue_task_command.
mission_items.enqueue_task_command enters _enqueue_task_unlocked, which generates item_id = BacklogItem.new_id() and passes root_task_id=item_id to manager_bounded_handoff.
The same pinned _enqueue_task_unlocked invocation explicitly passes name_session=False.

manager_dispatch.manager_bounded_handoff enters its naming classifier only when name_session is true; therefore this exact HTTP task route cannot activate that branch even though it supplies a generated non-null root_task_id.
bounded_slice.acceptance_effect: Exact-route negative evidence only. The pinned production HTTP task route preserves a generated mission/root id but hard-disables the bounded wrapper's name_session branch. This does not prove that no other production surface can call manager_bounded_handoff with name_session=true, and it does not negate unrelated reproduced Manager classification paths.
